name: Perfection
overview: Scripture presents perfection as a call to uprightness and sincerity in our walk with God, exemplified by Noah who was described as perfect in his generations because he walked with God (Genesis 6:9). God's command to Abram to "walk before me, and be thou perfect" (Genesis 17:1) and the exhortation in Deuteronomy to be perfect with the LORD (Deuteronomy 18:13) emphasize a life fully devoted to God’s standards. This perfection involves steadfast obedience without turning aside (Deuteronomy 5:32) and is characterized by God's presence with His people, as seen in His favorable regard for Jacob (Numbers 23:21). Thus, perfection in Scripture is not mere flawlessness but a sincere, upright relationship with God grounded in faithfulness and grace.
